rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one stepped compact mass, so it avoids the one-view-only failure. The dominant gesture is clear: a rectilinear slab turned into a terraced, ascending block. Hierarchy is legible, with a heavier base and a receding upper profile. The main weakness is that the verified access edge is not strongly transformed into a public void or entry seam; the mass mostly sits on the parcel rather than negotiating it. That keeps void_publicness low even though the form is otherwise stable. Programmatically, it can plausibly support neighborhood living/mixed-use because the massing suggests active lower levels and calm upper massing, and the stepped section is not in conflict with the brief. It is not especially ambitious as a public-building section, but it does not violate the contract. Reference resonance is strongest with the stepped mixed-use and terrace precedents, and weaker with the tower-like references, which are useful only as hierarchy comparisons.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked volumes with a readable central void and terrace-like setbacks can support mixed-use neighborhood massing.
A stepped/tapered profile can create a clear hierarchy while keeping the mass compact and legible.
